va_benefits.label: VA burial benefits (optional)
va_benefits.intro: If the deceased was a U.S. veteran, the VA may offset part of the cost. Amounts below are current for deaths on/after Oct 1, 2025.

allowances.label: VA burial allowance - service-connected death
allowances.detail: Up to $2,000 for deaths on/after Sept 11, 2001 ($1,500 if before). Deducted from the estimate.

allowances.label: VA burial + plot allowances - non-service-connected
allowances.detail: $1,002 burial allowance + $1,002 plot/interment allowance. Deducted from the estimate.

allowances.label: VA headstone / marker allowance (private cemetery)
allowances.detail: $441 toward a headstone or marker in a private cemetery. Optional add-on deduction.

va_benefits.national_cemetery: Burial in a VA national cemetery is free to the family: gravesite, opening and closing, government liner, headstone or marker, perpetual care of the gravesite, burial flag, Presidential Memorial Certificate, and military funeral honors. VA may also reimburse some transportation costs.
va_benefits.eligibility: Veteran discharged under conditions other than dishonorable, plus one qualifying condition (service-connected death, died while receiving VA care, etc.). The person who paid the costs claims it.
disclaimers: Benefits are NOT automatic - they must be claimed (VA Form 21P-530EZ). Non-service-connected claims must be filed within 2 years of burial.
Amounts reset every October 1 (start of the federal fiscal year). Verify current amounts at va.gov before planning.
Scam warning (AARP 2026): '$25,000 VA burial benefit' messages are fraudulent. Real allowances are up to $1,002 (non-service-connected) / $2,000 (service-connected).

upkeep.label: Cemetery upkeep - what 'perpetual care' really covers
upkeep.explainer: Most states require cemeteries to deposit a slice of each plot sale into a trust whose principal is held forever - e.g., California 10% or $250 (whichever is greater), Texas $1.75/sq ft or 15%. This is baked into the plot price, not a separate add-on, and it covers common grounds only (mowing, walkways, landscaping) - never your individual marker. Cleaning, straightening, or resetting a headstone is the family's responsibility and billed separately.

body_donation.label: Body donation to science (optional)
body_donation.intro: Whole-body donation programs typically cover cremation, transportation, and the death certificate at no cost, with cremated remains returned to the family. If accepted, the funeral-home portion of the estimate above would not apply.

programs.name: Science Care
programs.detail: Free cremation, transport of the body, and filing of the death certificate. Ashes typically returned in 3-5 weeks. No age limit; pre-registration not required.

programs.name: MedCure (nonprofit)
programs.detail: No-cost option covering transportation, one certified death certificate, cremation, and return of ashes or scattering at sea. No upper age limit.

catches: Open-casket funerals are NOT possible with whole-body donation; memorial services happen after the ashes are returned.
Final acceptance is decided AT THE TIME OF DEATH - pre-registration does not guarantee acceptance.
The body must be transferred to the program promptly; families are told not to engage a funeral home themselves at time of passing.
Common exclusions (MedCure): HIV/AIDS, hepatitis B/C, history of IV drug use, severe over/underweight at time of passing.
University willed-body programs follow the same general model, but return timelines (a semester to ~2 years) and transport radius vary by school - check the specific program.

cash_advance_note: Cash-advance items are third-party goods and services the funeral home passes through at cost: flowers, obituary notices, clergy honoraria, death certificates. Ranges on this site are industry-published typical ranges, not designed surveys, and vary by market.
